q: A microprocessor with 16 address lines can directly address a memory of
exp: 2^16 = 65,536 locations = 64 KB.

q: How many flags are present in the flag register of the 8085 microprocessor?
exp: The 8085 has five flags: Sign, Zero, Auxiliary Carry, Parity and Carry.

q: Which port of the 8051 microcontroller needs external pull-up resistors when used as a general-purpose I/O port?
exp: Port 0 has open-drain outputs, so external pull-ups are needed for ordinary I/O use.

q: Which blocks are integrated on a single-chip microcontroller but are NOT part of the microprocessor (CPU) itself?
options: ROM/Flash, RAM, timers and I/O ports
exp: A microcontroller = CPU + memory + peripherals on one chip; the microprocessor is only the CPU.

q: Which of the following is a typical embedded application of a microcontroller?
exp: A washing machine controller is a dedicated, low-cost control task, which is what microcontrollers are designed for.

q: The 8086 has 20 address lines. Its physical memory space is therefore
In the I/O-mapped I/O scheme of the 8085, how many input ports can be addressed?
exp: IN and OUT instructions carry an 8-bit port address, so 2^8 = 256 input ports (and 256 output ports) are possible.

q: Which 8085 instruction loads the accumulator from a memory location whose 16-bit address is given directly in the instruction?
exp: LDA addr (direct addressing, 3 bytes) copies the byte at the given address into A.

q: How many 16-bit timer/counters are available in the standard 8051?
exp: The 8051 has Timer 0 and Timer 1; the 8052 adds Timer 2.

q: The Harvard architecture, used by the 8051, PIC and AVR families, has
options: one common memory for program and data
separate memories and buses for program and data
only a cache and no main memory
exp: Harvard architecture keeps program and data in separate memories, allowing simultaneous fetch of instruction and data; von Neumann uses a single memory.

q: Which interrupt of the 8085 has the highest priority?
exp: TRAP is non-maskable and has the highest priority, followed by RST 7.5, 6.5, 5.5 and INTR.

q: Which of the following is a control flag in the 8086 flag register?
exp: The control flags of the 8086 are TF, IF and DF; ZF, CF and AF are status flags.

q: An 8-bit ADC in a microcontroller uses a 5 V reference. The number of distinct digital output codes is
exp: An n-bit ADC has 2^n codes: 2^8 = 256, so each step is about 5/256 = 19.5 mV.

q: A microcontroller differs from a microprocessor mainly because a microcontroller integrates on one chip
options: CPU along with RAM, ROM, timers and I/O ports
exp: A microcontroller is a computer on a chip: CPU plus memory and peripherals, whereas a microprocessor is essentially only the CPU.

q: In an 8085 program, MVI A,45H is followed by ADI 3BH. What is the content of A and the Carry flag after ADI?
exp: 45H + 3BH = 80H, which fits in 8 bits, so no carry is generated (CY = 0).

q: What is the size of the instruction prefetch queue of the 8086?
exp: The 8086 has a 6-byte queue (the 8088 has a 4-byte queue).

q: The internal data RAM of the 8051 is
exp: The 8051 has 128 bytes of on-chip data RAM (the 8052 has 256 bytes).

q: Which description fits ARM processors?
options: 8-bit CISC chips with high power consumption
32-bit RISC cores with low power consumption
exp: ARM cores are low-power RISC designs that dominate mobile phones and embedded devices.

q: The instruction MOV AX,[BX+SI+08H] in the 8086 uses which addressing mode?
exp: A base register (BX), an index register (SI) and an 8-bit displacement are all added, which is based indexed addressing with displacement.

q: Which of the 8085 interrupts is a non-vectored interrupt, i.e. the interrupting device must supply the instruction/vector?
exp: INTR is non-vectored; the external device places an RST or CALL opcode on the data bus in response to INTA. The others have fixed vector addresses.

q: In the 8086, CS = 2000H and IP = 0150H. What is the physical address of the next instruction?
exp: Physical address = CS x 16 + IP = 20000H + 0150H = 20150H.

q: What is the interrupt vector (ROM) address of the Timer 1 overflow interrupt in the 8051?
exp: 8051 vectors: INT0 0003H, Timer 0 000BH, INT1 0013H, Timer 1 001BH, Serial 0023H.

q: Which statement about memory-mapped I/O is correct?
options: It uses only the IN and OUT instructions
The number of ports is limited to 256
I/O devices are treated like memory locations, so memory-reference instructions can be used on them
It does not reduce the memory space available for memory
exp: In memory-mapped I/O devices share the memory address space, so any memory instruction (MOV, ADD, etc.) can access them, at the cost of memory space.

q: After executing XRA A in an 8085 program, the Zero and Carry flags are
exp: A XOR A = 0, so Z = 1; XRA always clears CY.

q: A UART in a microcontroller is used for
exp: The Universal Asynchronous Receiver/Transmitter sends and receives serial frames with start and stop bits and no shared clock.

q: In a hard real-time embedded system
options: a missed deadline only slightly degrades quality
a missed deadline can be a system failure
exp: Hard real-time systems must meet deadlines absolutely; missing one is treated as failure (e.g. airbag control).

q: Which pair correctly gives (data bus width, address bus width) of the 8086?
exp: The 8086 has a 16-bit data bus (AD0-AD15) and 20 address lines.

q: In the 8051 PSW, RS1 RS0 = 1 0 selects the register bank located at
exp: Bank 0 = 00H-07H, bank 1 = 08H-0FH, bank 2 = 10H-17H, bank 3 = 18H-1FH; RS1 RS0 = 10 selects bank 2.

q: In an 8086 program, AX = 0064H and BL = 07H. After DIV BL, the registers hold
exp: 100 / 7 gives quotient 14 (0EH) in AL and remainder 2 in AH.

q: An 8-bit ADC has a reference of 2.56 V. For an input of 1.00 V the digital output (in decimal) is
An 8051 runs from a 12 MHz crystal. Timer 1 in Mode 1 is to give a 1 ms delay. The value to load in TH1:TL1 is
exp: Machine cycle = 1 microsecond, so 1000 counts are needed: 65536 - 1000 = 64536 = FC18H.

q:
Statement I: In the 8085 the stack pointer is a 16-bit register.
Statement II: In the 8085 the stack grows towards lower memory addresses.
Which is correct?
exp: SP is 16 bits wide and PUSH decrements it by 2, so the stack grows downward.

q: Which register of a microprocessor holds the address of the next instruction to be fetched?
exp: The program counter (IP in the 8086) points to the next instruction and is updated after each fetch.

q: In the 8085, SP = 2000H and PUSH B is executed. What is the new SP and where is register C stored?
exp: PUSH stores B at SP-1 = 1FFFH and C at SP-2 = 1FFEH, then SP becomes 1FFEH.
